newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-JONES CRUISES THROUGH FIRST ROUND OF 100 METRES.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-JONES CRUISES THROUGH FIRST ROUND OF 100 METRES.

text.p: American Marion Jones, favourite for the women's world 100 metres title, cruised through the opening round on Saturday then said she was delighted the race was out of the way.
Jones won her heat in 11.09 seconds, third fastest time in the first round.
"I could hardly sleep last night I was so excited," said the 21-year-old American champion.
"But now I have run that feels like just another race. I don't feel so nervous. These are my first world championships and a lot of people have been watching me to see how I react, but I feel fine."
Zhanna Pintussevich of Ukraine was the fastest qualifier with 11.01, while American Inger Miller was another impressive winner, taking her heat in 11.07 seconds.

The evergreen Merlene Ottey of Jamaica, who has won more world championship medals than any other athlete but who is still seeking her first 100 gold, also came through without trouble, winning her heat in 11.27 seconds.
Thirty-two women will take part in the second round later on Saturday, but they will not include Marwa Rostom of Palestine.
The 14-year-old, born in the year of the first world championships in 1983 and the youngest here, did not start her race.
